Handspring website, 2000

Handspring’s home page in August 2000, led by a large photograph of a translucent blue Visor.

www.handspring.com (archived copy)

Rights
Third-party work, stored with credit for commentary. License: unverified. Rights policy

Observed

  • A large photograph at upper left shows a translucent blue Visor at an angle, with round silver buttons, on a blue textured surface that curves away in a swoosh.
  • “VISOR” is set in large serif capitals that fade from pale blue to dark blue; the tagline “whatever the heck you want it to be.” is in small blue sans-serif.
  • Three columns start with lilac tab bars whose ends are rounded: “places to go”, “things to buy”, and “news to know”, with the last word in heavy blue.
  • Product teasers pair small photos (an orange Visor, a thin modem, colored styluses, a leather case) with light lilac headings.
  • Small orange “GO” circles and square lilac and green buttons act as controls. A blue textured swoosh closes the layout at the bottom.

Why it belongs

The site sells the object that carries the style: the Visor in translucent candy colors. The page shows the product photo as the hero and repeats its blue and rounded shapes in the tab bars.

Measured: no CSS gradients, shadows, or radii; the pixel palette is mostly white with a strong blue accent.

Borrow

Use a product photo on a curved band of color as the page header, and echo the curve in the footer.
